newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Gilt gains to slow after break,113-19 key.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Gilt gains to slow after break,113-19 key.

text.p: June gilt futures technically look bullish after their major upbreak on Tuesday but the market needs to show it can sustain its brief move above the old contract high at 113-19, analysts said on Wednesday.

They said in the short term gilts may be susceptible to declines amid profit-taking, especially after the strength of their recent run. On Tuesday, gilts rose more than two full points to post their biggest one-day gain in five years.
"Short-term the market is very overbought," said Francoise Skelley, head of global trading technical analysis at Credit Suisse First Boston in London.
June gilts at 0707 GMT were at 113-09, down 4/32.
Skelley said the market could slip back all the way towards 111-16 but she was bullish on its prospects further out.

Speaking on Reuters Financial Television, she noted a major downtrend since 1986 as shown on monthly continuation charts. That trend resistance came in around the 117-118 area and would be the target of an extended move higher.
Meantime, there was resistance at 114-05, Skelley said.
Elizabeth Miller, technical analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London, noted that was a continuation chart high in mid-February, and beyond there she saw resistance at 115-26.
Miller said 115-26 was a 76.4 percent Fibonacci retracement of the decline from 121-06, a high on monthly continuation charts at the end of 1993.
"Really it looks pretty good at the moment but it's got to sustain a break of 113-19. Gains from here are going to be a lot slower," she said.
On the downside, she pegged immediate support on 30-minute charts at 112-25 and said 112-13 was small retracement level.
September short sterling was at 93.18, down 0.01. The short contracts all along the strip also rallied on Tuesday. Similarly they were a little more subdued on Wednesday, analysts said.
